edit.description: a merged entry's slot provisions the next entry the selection hands it on its own — its own `createWorktree` base, its own `setupWorktree` — then invokes it, and the wave ends on the selection rather than on its first batch
the next pickable entry disjoint from what is still in flight, off the collision read the batch partition already makes
the refill arms, beside the batch-width cases

summary: The width a merged entry releases sits idle until the whole wave settles: nothing refills a freed slot, and the tick ends at its first batch

per.section: Fanout and worktrees — provisioning, isolation, teardown

acceptance: a slot freed by a merged entry pulls the next pickable entry disjoint from everything still in flight and provisions it alone as it is pulled — cut from the tip it is pulled at, its `setupWorktree` run there, its decline consulted after both — and the tick ends when nothing is pickable or its budget says to put the wave down rather than when one batch has drained
tests: a slot freed by a merged entry pulls the next pickable entry disjoint from what is still in flight
an entry a freed slot pulls is provisioned from the tip it is pulled at rather than the tip the wave started on
a wave keeps pulling pickable entries until none remain rather than ending with its first batch
notes: Half two of the ruling; chained rather than seamed because the refill is written against the per-entry merge's own completion. The refill wants `partitionByFileOverlap`'s one-entry form against the in-flight set (`src/selection.ts:359`).
